primary_source_screen.finding: 2025 total factor productivity rose in 7 of 19 major industries; 12 of 19 had output-price growth faster than combined input prices. Annual retrospective data, not an AI causal estimate.
Q3 2026 nonfarm labour productivity +3.6% annualized; unit labour costs -0.7% annualized and +2.4% year on year; preliminary.

primary_source_screen.institution: Federal Reserve Board, Governor Lisa D. Cook
primary_source_screen.finding: More than US$2tn in announced U.S. data-centre construction projects, only a fraction realized; roughly half of capacity under construction estimated outside the U.S.; individual governor speech, not FOMC decision.

primary_source_screen.institution: National Bureau of Statistics of China
primary_source_screen.finding: October industrial value added +4.8%, high-tech manufacturing +17.6%; Jan-Oct fixed investment -8.1%, private investment -11.4%; October consumer-goods retail sales +0.4%.
September net TIC inflow US$261bn, private inflows US$267bn and official outflows US$6bn; lagged, custodial and not evidence of flows after 20 November.

Corporate financing costs rose, credit volumes remained resilient but lost momentum, banks tightened lending standards; concentrated AI exposures and non-bank liquidity/leverage risks are vulnerabilities, not evidence of a generalized credit freeze.
October CPI +2.3% y/y; excluding fresh food +2.2%; excluding fresh food and energy +2.2%.
Flash consumer-confidence indicator improved 1.0 point to -16.9 but remained below long-term average.
Euro-area October flash annual inflation 4.0%, with energy component 20.8% y/y.
Copom held Selic at 13.75%; noted activity moderation, inflation acceleration and expectations at 5.2% for 2026 and 4.8% for 2027.
October IPCA +0.14% m/m after +0.82% in September; monthly moderation does not remove expectation risk.
October global oil supply estimated at 105.4 mb/d; observed inventories +52m barrels; 2026 demand forecast down 2.7 mb/d to 102.3 mb/d; diesel and freight constraints remain.

primary_source_screen.institution: ECDC and WHO Regional Office for Europe
primary_source_screen.finding: New 2025 human invasive-isolate AMR data from EARS-Net and CAESAR. In 21 of 43 reporting countries, at least half of K. pneumoniae samples were resistant to third-generation cephalosporins; not veterinary surveillance.
Rapid risk assessment reports worsening CRE situation and rising incidence of carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae bloodstream infections in EU/EEA; human health assessment.
October Food Price Index 133.9, down 1.2% m/m but 5.9% above a year earlier; international commodity basket, not household affordability or diet quality.
Bundibugyo update as of 17 Nov: 11,613 confirmed cases, 5,678 deaths, 720 deaths since 28 Oct; 452 community deaths; PHEIC reaffirmed 18 Nov; contact follow-up average 81%, below 95% threshold.
BWC Working Group tenth session scheduled for 7–11 December; upcoming governance process, not a new treaty outcome or compliance finding.

decision: MT-GM-2026-11-22 was absent at the initial HEAD and is staged as revision 2 with schema v2 ready:true; QA and public approval remain pending. No additional thematic article was created: the WHO 20 November Bundibugyo update is already covered by the 21 November thematic item; the new WHO/ECDC AMR release concerns human invasive isolates and does not supply a new veterinary/livestock delta. MT-GM-2026-11-19 remains rejected revision 3, while revision 4 was blocked under the no-fourth-rejection rule; revision 5 now corrects the four material source-traceability issues (final U.S. index values and semiconductor direction, exact Reuters oil-wire source, Asian closing data, and source-audit counts) and is pending independent QA. No fourth rejection was recorded; ID and slug are unchanged.
limitations: The 63 active registry assets were reconciled operationally, including every editorial line and tool/program entry. This is not an exhaustive primary-source investigation of every line. Human AMR surveillance is not treated as livestock evidence; outbreak figures retain their stated cutoff; conflict claims retain source attribution; no unsupported actor, cause or biosecurity allegation is promoted to fact.
